function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times (e.g., Thales of Miletus noted static electricity from amber). The first systematic scientific study of it was carried out by **William Gilbert** in the early 1600s, who coined the term *electricus* and distinguished magnetism from static electricity. Subsequent key figures include Benjamin Franklin (electrostatic experiments), Alessandro Volta (the voltaic pile), and many others who built on Gilbert’s work to develop our modern understanding of electricity.
